name: Gṛtsamada
summary: Seer of most of Ṛgveda book 2 (e.g. 2.12 on Indra, whom some say 'does not exist' — 'have faith in him'; 2.33 to Rudra the best of physicians). The Anukramaṇī calls him formerly Āṅgirasa Śaunahotra, later Bhārgava Śaunaka.

realization_account.text: The tradition counts him among the seers who 'saw' the hymns of the second maṇḍala.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Viśvāmitra
summary: Viśvāmitra Gāthina of the Kuśika clan, seer of Ṛgveda book 3, including the Gāyatrī (3.62.10) and the dialogue in which the rivers Vipāś and Śutudrī yield to his words (3.33; the rivers themselves are counted as seers of their verses). Priest of King Sudās in book 3; the tradition makes him the rival of Vasiṣṭha and, in the epics, a king who became a brahmarṣi through tapas.

realization_account.text: Born a kṣatriya king (son of Gādhi), he attained the status of brahmarṣi by long tapas and was at last acknowledged by Vasiṣṭha (Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (epic)

notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). The Rāmāyaṇa episode is recalled at book level only.

name: Vāmadeva
summary: Vāmadeva Gautama, seer of Ṛgveda book 4. His verses 'I was Manu and I the Sun' (4.26.1) and 'while still in the womb I knew all the births of the gods' (4.27.1) are cited in the Upaniṣads as the words of one who realized himself as all (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.10; Aitareya 2.5).

realization_account.text: Seeing this (the self as brahman), the seer Vāmadeva attained it and said 'I was Manu, and the Sun'; knowing in the womb the births of the gods, he rose from the body and, attaining all desires in heaven, became immortal.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (Upaniṣads)

notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). The Anukramaṇī allows Indra (or the self, ātman) as speaker/deity of 4.26.1–3.

name: Atri
summary: Atri Bhauma, founder of the Ātreya family whose hymns form Ṛgveda book 5 (e.g. 5.85, Varuṇa's great māyā); one of the seven seers of RV 10.137. Later tradition makes him husband of Anasūyā and father of Dattātreya.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Bharadvāja
summary: Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya, founder of the family of Ṛgveda book 6, whose vision of the light set in the heart (6.9.5–6) is among the Veda's inner experiences; one of the seven seers of RV 10.137.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Vasiṣṭha
summary: Vasiṣṭha Maitrāvaruṇi, seer of Ṛgveda book 7: the hymns to Varuṇa in which he searches his conscience (7.86–89), the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya verse (7.59.12), the account of his birth from Mitra-Varuṇa and Urvaśī, 'born from mind' (7.33.11), and the victory of King Sudās in the Battle of the Ten Kings (7.18, 7.33). The tradition makes him the Ikṣvāku family priest and teacher of Rāma, rival and finally acknowledger of Viśvāmitra.

realization_account.text: Varuṇa took Vasiṣṭha into his boat and made him a seer by his powers (RV 7.88.3–4).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (Ṛgveda)

notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). Parāśara is his grandson (through Śakti) in the tradition; 'students' here records that line of descent.

name: Kaṇva
summary: Kaṇva Ghaura, seer of RV 1.36–43 (incl. 1.43 to Rudra 'lord of songs, lord of sacrifice, with the healing jalāṣa'); eponym of the Kāṇva family whose hymns fill most of book 8.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Dīrghatamas
summary: Dīrghatamas Aucathya (Māmateya), seer of RV 1.140–164, including the riddle hymn 1.164 (the two birds, the four quarters of speech, 'the One Being the inspired call by many names'), the Viṣṇu hymn 1.154 and the horse-sacrifice hymns 1.162–163. The tradition remembers him as born blind.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). 'Born blind' and 'father of Kakṣīvant' are traditional (Bṛhaddevatā/epic) reports recalled with moderate confidence.

name: Agastya
summary: Agastya Maitrāvaruṇi, seer of RV 1.165–191; in 1.179 he answers his wife Lopāmudrā, reconciling long tapas with married life, and is said to have 'nourished both colours'. Born with Vasiṣṭha of Mitra-Varuṇa in the tradition; the Tamil tradition identifies him with the Siddhar Agastya (the Vedic contribution is recorded here).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). Scholars do not assume the Vedic and Tamil Agastyas are one person.

name: Lopāmudrā
summary: Wife of Agastya and seer of RV 1.179.1–2: after many autumns of toil she laments that age wears away the beauty of bodies and asks that husbands come to their wives; the ancient seers too, who spoke truths with the gods, did not reach the end (of tapas).
notes: Named among the brahmavādinīs of the Bṛhaddevatā. The Śākta (Śrīvidyā) tradition names a Lopāmudrā as seer of one form of the Śrīvidyā mantra (reference only, low confidence).

name: Madhucchandas
summary: Madhucchandas Vaiśvāmitra, son of Viśvāmitra, seer of the opening hymns of the Ṛgveda (1.1–10: 'I praise Agni, the household priest…') and of the opening of the Soma book (9.1).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Medhātithi Kāṇva
summary: Seer of RV 1.12–23, including 1.22.20: 'the wise ever see that highest step of Viṣṇu, like an eye stretched out in heaven'.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Śunaḥśepa
summary: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti, later adopted as Devarāta Vaiśvāmitra, seer of RV 1.24–30, including the prayer that Varuṇa loosen the upper, middle and lower fetters so that we may be sinless before Aditi (1.24.15). His rescue from being sacrificed is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa narrative (7.13–18) is cited from memory.

name: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa
summary: Seer of RV 1.31–35, including the Indra–Vṛtra hymn 1.32 ('I will proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra…').
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Praskaṇva Kāṇva
summary: Seer of RV 1.44–50, ending with the Sūrya hymn 1.50 ('from the darkness we have come up … to the highest light').
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Gotama Rāhūgaṇa
summary: Seer of RV 1.74–93, including 1.89 ('let auspicious intentions come to us from every side') and 1.90.9 ('may Mitra be propitious to us…').
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Kutsa Āṅgirasa
summary: Seer of RV 1.94–98 and 1.101–115, including the Rudra hymn 1.114 and 1.115.1 ('Sūrya is the self of what moves and what stands'); the Atharvaveda hymn to the highest Brahman (AVŚ 10.8) is also ascribed to Kutsa.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Kakṣīvant
summary: Kakṣīvant Dairghatamasa Auśija, seer of RV 1.116–126 (hymns to the Aśvins and gift-praises); father of the ṛṣikā Ghoṣā.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Parāśara
summary: Parāśara Śāktya, seer of RV 1.65–73 (hymns to Agni). The tradition makes him the son of Śakti and grandson of Vasiṣṭha, father of Vyāsa, and the narrator of the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (the Vedic contribution is recorded here).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Nema Bhārgava
summary: Seer of RV 8.100.1–3, 6–12, in which 'Nema says Indra does not exist — who has seen him? whom shall we praise?', whereupon Indra answers 'here I am, singer, see me' (8.100.3–4).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Kaśyapa
summary: Kaśyapa Mārīca, seer of RV 1.99 and of the closing Soma hymns 9.113–114 (the prayer to be made immortal in the world of unfading light and bliss); one of the seven seers of RV 10.137; in the Atharvaveda 'self-born Kaśyapa' arises from Time (AVŚ 19.53.10).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Jamadagni
summary: Jamadagni Bhārgava, seer of hymns in books 8–10 (e.g. 8.101) and of 'the waters are healing' in the seven-seer hymn (10.137.6); in the Purāṇas the father of Paraśurāma.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Bhṛgu
summary: Eponymous ancestor of the Bhārgava priests; with the Aṅgirases the source of the Atharvaveda (Bhṛgvaṅgirasaḥ); in the Ṛgveda the Bhṛgus are among those who brought fire to men.

name: Aṅgiras
summary: Eponymous ancestor of the Āṅgirasa priests; the Atharvaveda is 'the Atharvans and the Aṅgirases' (Atharvāṅgirasaḥ), the aṅgiras hymns being traditionally the fierce (ābhicārika) and the atharvan hymns the auspicious (bheṣaja) portion.
notes: The division of the Atharvaveda into atharvan (auspicious) and āṅgirasa (fierce) portions is a traditional and scholarly account recalled with moderate confidence. The Aṅgiras who teaches Śaunaka in the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad is a separate figure in U03's scope.

name: Atharvan
summary: The primordial fire-priest: 'you, Agni, Atharvan churned forth from the lotus' (RV 6.16.13); eponym and seer of many Atharvaveda hymns (e.g. AVŚ 1.1, 3.30, 10.7, 11.7, 12.1, 15).

name: Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa
summary: Seer of the hymn on knowledge and speech (RV 10.71) and, with alternatives, of the hymn on the birth of the gods (10.72).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Nārāyaṇa (seer of the Puruṣa Sūkta)
summary: The seer of the Puruṣa Sūkta (RV 10.90) and of the Atharvaveda hymn on the making of man (AVŚ 10.2); Vaiṣṇava tradition identifies him with Nārāyaṇa, the Lord.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin
summary: The seer to whom the Anukramaṇī ascribes the creation hymn (RV 10.129).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Hiraṇyagarbha Prājāpatya
summary: The seer to whom the Anukramaṇī ascribes the Hiraṇyagarbha hymn (RV 10.121); the deity is Ka, i.e. Prajāpati.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Vāc Āmbhṛṇī
summary: Vāc, daughter of the seer Ambhṛṇa, the ṛṣikā of RV 10.125, in which Speech proclaims herself the queen and self of all, moving with the gods, the power by which beings eat, see, breathe and hear, who makes whom she loves a brahman and a seer.

realization_account.text: The Anukramaṇī gives the deity of her hymn as 'ātman', the seer praising herself as the self of all; later commentary (Sāyaṇa) presents her as a knower of Brahman who spoke from identity with it.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). Sāyaṇa's characterization recalled with moderate confidence.

name: Viśvakarman Bhauvana
summary: Seer (and deity) of the Viśvakarman hymns RV 10.81–82.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Aghamarṣaṇa Mādhucchandasa
summary: Seer of RV 10.190 (ṛta and satya born of tapas), the 'sin-effacing' verses recited at the bath.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Yama Vaivasvata
summary: Son of Vivasvant, the first mortal to die and find the path for many to the fathers; king of the dead in the highest heaven; seer of RV 10.14 and of his verses in the Yama–Yamī dialogue (10.10).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Yamī Vaivasvatī
summary: Yama's twin sister, speaker of her verses in RV 10.10 and ṛṣikā of 10.154 (on the departed who reached heaven by tapas).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Śraddhā Kāmāyanī
summary: The ṛṣikā of the hymn to Faith (RV 10.151).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Sūryā Sāvitrī
summary: Daughter of Savitṛ, the ṛṣikā of the wedding hymn RV 10.85, which opens 'by truth the earth is upheld' and distinguishes the pressed soma from the soma the brahmins know.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Ghoṣā Kākṣīvatī
summary: Daughter of Kakṣīvant, ṛṣikā of RV 10.39–40 to the Aśvins; the tradition says she remained unmarried in her father's house through a skin disease until the Aśvins healed her.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). The illness story is the commentarial account (moderate confidence).

name: Apālā Ātreyī
summary: ṛṣikā of RV 8.91: a maiden who found soma on her way to the water, offered it to Indra and was freed by him of a skin affliction.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Viśvavārā Ātreyī
summary: ṛṣikā of RV 5.28, a hymn to Agni kindled at dawn as she offers to the gods.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Juhū Brahmajāyā
summary: ṛṣikā (with Ūrdhvanābhā Brāhma as alternative) of RV 10.109 on the restoration of the brahmin's wife.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Śacī Paulomī
summary: Indra's consort, ṛṣikā of RV 10.159, in which she praises herself as victorious.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Indrāṇī
summary: Speaker in the Vṛṣākapi hymn (RV 10.86) and ṛṣikā of RV 10.145, a charm against a co-wife.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Sārparājñī
summary: The 'serpent queen', ṛṣikā of RV 10.189 (the dappled bull who has come; deity ātman or the Sun).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Romaśā
summary: ṛṣikā of RV 1.126.7.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Śaśvatī Āṅgirasī
summary: ṛṣikā of RV 8.1.34.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Rātri Bhāradvājī
summary: Named (beside Kuśika Saubhara) as ṛṣikā of the hymn to Night, RV 10.127.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Dakṣiṇā Prājāpatyā
summary: Named (beside Divya Āṅgirasa) as ṛṣikā of the hymn in praise of the sacrificial gift, RV 10.107.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Godhā
summary: ṛṣikā of RV 10.134.6b–7.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Aditi Dākṣāyaṇī
summary: Named as one possible seer of RV 10.72 on the birth of the gods (Aditi born of Dakṣa and Dakṣa of Aditi).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Agastya's sister (mother of the Gaupāyanas)
summary: ṛṣikā of RV 10.60.6; named among the brahmavādinīs of the Bṛhaddevatā.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Urvaśī
summary: The apsaras whose dialogue with King Purūravas forms RV 10.95; ṛṣikā of her verses.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Kavaṣa Ailūṣa
summary: Seer of RV 10.30–34 (with Akṣa Maujavant as alternative for the gambler's hymn 10.34). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa tells that the seers drove him from a sacrificial session as 'son of a slave woman', until the waters followed him and they accepted him as one known to the gods.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa episode (2.19) is recalled with moderate confidence.

name: Bhiṣag Ātharvaṇa
summary: The 'physician, son of Atharvan', seer of the hymn to healing plants RV 10.97.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Bhikṣu Āṅgirasa
summary: Seer of RV 10.117 on the giving of wealth and food ('he who eats alone has only sin').
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Saṃvanana Āṅgirasa
summary: Seer of RV 10.191, the closing hymn of concord.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Laba Aindra
summary: Seer of RV 10.119, the soma-exalted self-praise with the refrain 'have I not drunk of the soma?'; the Anukramaṇī gives its deity as ātman (Indra).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: The Vātaraśana munis (seven wind-girdled sages)
summary: The seven 'wind-girdled' silent sages to whom the verses of the Keśin hymn (RV 10.136) are ascribed one each: Jūti, Vātajūti, Viprajūti, Vṛṣāṇaka, Karikrata, Etaśa and Ṛśyaśṛṅga.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked). A group entry.

name: Manu Vaivasvata
summary: Son of Vivasvant, ancestor of humankind, seer of RV 8.27–31. (Distinct in the tradition from Manu Svāyambhuva of the Manusmṛti.)
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Vena Bhārgava
summary: Seer of the Vena hymn RV 10.123; in the Atharvaveda (2.1) and Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (32.8) Vena is the seer who 'saw that highest, hidden in secret, in which all becomes one nest'.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Śyāvāśva Ātreya
summary: Seer of RV 5.81 to Savitṛ, which opens 'the inspired yoke their mind and yoke their thoughts' (5.81.1).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Garga Bhāradvāja
summary: Seer of RV 6.47, including 'Indra goes in many forms by his māyās' (6.47.18).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Medhya Kāṇva
summary: Seer of the Vālakhilya hymn RV 8.58: 'one Agni kindled in many ways … one has become all this'.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Pragātha Ghaura Kāṇva
summary: Seer of RV 8.1.1–2 and 8.48, 'we have drunk the soma, we have become immortal'.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Pavitra Āṅgirasa
summary: Seer of RV 9.83: the filter of the lord of sacred speech is spread out; the raw one whose body is unheated does not attain it.
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Bhārgava Vaidarbhi
summary: The seer to whom the Prāṇa hymn of the Atharvaveda (AVŚ 11.4) is ascribed.
notes: Ascription taken from the hymn header of the local Atharvaveda text (checked).

name: Nārada
summary: In the Saṃhitās, Nārada Kāṇva is seer of RV 8.13 and, with Parvata, of the Soma hymns 9.104–105; the Sāmaveda phonetic manual (Nāradīya Śikṣā) is ascribed to Nārada (the Vedic contributions only are recorded here).
notes: Seer attributions follow the Sarvānukramaṇī as printed in the hymn headers of the local Ṛgveda text (checked).

name: Vyāsa (Veda-vyāsa)
summary: Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, son of Parāśara, called Veda-vyāsa, 'arranger of the Veda': seeing the decline of the ages, he divided the one Veda into four for the continuity of the sacrifice and taught the Ṛg to Paila, the Sāma to Jaimini, the Yajus to Vaiśampāyana and the Atharva to Sumantu, who branched them into śākhās through their pupils (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4.19–23; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.4).

realization_account.text: Having divided the Veda and composed the Mahābhārata for those not entitled to hear the Veda, he was still not content until he composed the Bhāgavata (BhP 1.4.25–1.5).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (Purāṇa)

notes: U01 contribution: Vyāsa as divider of the Veda. Other units contribute Vyāsa as author of the Mahābhārata, Brahma Sūtras (as Bādarāyaṇa in some traditions) and Purāṇas.

name: Paila
summary: Vyāsa's pupil who received the Ṛgveda (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4.21; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.4) and divided it among his own pupils, from whom the Ṛgveda śākhās descend.

name: Vaiśampāyana
summary: Vyāsa's pupil who received the Yajurveda and made twenty-seven branches of it (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.5.1); teacher of Yājñavalkya, whose disgorged Yajus the other pupils took up as partridges (tittiri) — hence the Taittirīyas; narrator of the Mahābhārata to Janamejaya.

name: Jaimini
summary: Vyāsa's pupil who received the Sāmaveda (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4.21); eponym of the Jaiminīya Sāmaveda. The tradition identifies him with the author of the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra (the identification is disputed by scholars).
notes: U01 contribution: the Sāmaveda transmitter.

name: Sumantu
summary: Vyāsa's pupil who received the Atharvaveda ('the fierce sage of the Atharvāṅgirasas', Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4.22).

name: Yājñavalkya
summary: Son of Brahmarāta, pupil of Vaiśampāyana. Told to give back what he had learned after offering to perform an expiation alone, he disgorged the Yajus; then, devoted to breath-control, he praised the Sun as the door of liberation and received from the Sun, in the form of a horse (vājin), Yajus unknown to his teacher — the White Yajurveda of the Vājasaneyins (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.5).

realization_account.text: The Sun, as a horse, granted him the 'unused' (ayātayāma) Yajus not known to his teacher (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.5.26–29).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (Purāṇa)

notes: U01 contribution: the White Yajurveda revelation. U03 contributes the Upaniṣadic teacher.

name: Tittiri
summary: Eponym of the Taittirīya school. The Purāṇa derives the name from Vaiśampāyana's pupils who became partridges (tittiri) to take up the disgorged Yajus (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.5.13); the grammatical tradition derives it from a teacher named Tittiri (Pāṇini 4.3.102).
notes: The Pāṇini sūtra number is recalled from memory (moderate).

name: Kaṭha
summary: Pupil of Vaiśampāyana and eponym of the Kaṭha (Kāṭhaka) branch of the Black Yajurveda.

name: Śākalya
summary: The teacher credited with the Padapāṭha of the Ṛgveda and eponym of the Śākala recension; cited by Yāska and Pāṇini. Tradition sometimes identifies him with Vidagdha Śākalya, Yājñavalkya's questioner on the number of the gods in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka (3.9) — an identification scholars dispute.

name: Bāṣkala
summary: Eponym of the Bāṣkala recension of the Ṛgveda, named in the Purāṇic accounts among the pupils in Paila's line.
notes: Position in the pupil lists recalled from memory (low).

name: Śaunaka
summary: The ancient teacher to whom the tradition ascribes the Śaunaka recension of the Atharvaveda and the Ṛgveda ancillaries — the Ṛgveda Prātiśākhya, the Anukramaṇīs, the Bṛhaddevatā and the Ṛgvidhāna — and whom it makes the teacher of Āśvalāyana. Whether these are one Śaunaka, and whether he is the Śaunaka of the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad or of the Naimiṣa forest in the epics, is not settled.

name: Pippalāda
summary: Eponym of the Paippalāda Atharvaveda; the teacher of the Praśna Upaniṣad (U03 contributes that role).

name: Kātyāyana
summary: The ancient ritualist and phonetician to whom the Sarvānukramaṇī of the Ṛgveda, the Vājasaneyi Prātiśākhya and the Śrauta Sūtra of the White Yajurveda are ascribed; the tradition often identifies him with Kātyāyana the critic of Pāṇini (disputed).

name: Yāska
summary: Author of the Nirukta, the etymological commentary on the Vedic word-lists (Nighaṇṭu). He defends the meaningfulness of the mantras against Kautsa (Nirukta 1.15–16), teaches that the seers had direct vision of dharma (1.20), that one who recites the Veda without knowing its meaning is a post bearing a load (1.18), and that because of the deity's greatness the one Self is praised in many ways (7.4).

scholarly.text: c. 6th–5th century BCE (before Pāṇini, low confidence)

notes: U01 contribution (Yāska as interpreter of the Saṃhitās); U02 owns the Nirukta.

name: Kautsa
summary: The teacher whose view that 'the mantras are meaningless' (anarthakā hi mantrāḥ) Yāska states and refutes (Nirukta 1.15–16).

name: Vyāḍi
summary: Ancient grammarian; the Vikṛtivallī on the eight modified recitations is ascribed to him.
notes: Ascription of the Vikṛtivallī recalled with low confidence.

name: Sāyaṇa
summary: Sāyaṇa (Sāyaṇācārya), minister of the early Vijayanagara kings and director of the great series of Vedic commentaries (Vedārthaprakāśa) on the Saṃhitās, Brāhmaṇas and Āraṇyakas, which explain the hymns chiefly by their ritual use; also author of digests (the 'Sudhānidhi' works).
notes: Brother of Mādhava, whom the tradition identifies with Vidyāraṇya (tch:vidyaranya) — identification disputed. Birth year unknown; 'from' is a rough estimate.

name: Skandasvāmin
summary: Author of an early Ṛgveda commentary (partly surviving) and, with Maheśvara, a commentary on the Nirukta.
notes: Reported as teacher of Harisvāmin, commentator on the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (low confidence).

name: Veṅkaṭamādhava
summary: Author of the Ṛgarthadīpikā, a concise commentary on the whole Ṛgveda.

name: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara Miśra
summary: Author of the Jñānayajña, commentary on the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka.

name: Uvaṭa
summary: Son of Vajraṭa of Ānandapura; wrote at Avantī under King Bhoja a commentary (Mantrabhāṣya) on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā and a commentary on the Ṛgveda Prātiśākhya.

name: Mahīdhara
summary: Vārāṇasī scholar who wrote the Vedadīpa on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā; the same Mahīdhara compiled the tantric manual Mantramahodadhi.

name: Madhva (Ānandatīrtha)
summary: U01 contribution: author of the Ṛgbhāṣya on RV 1.1–40, reading the hymns as ultimately praising Viṣṇu, the one denoted by all names.

name: Dayānanda Sarasvatī
summary: Founder of the Ārya Samāj (1875); commented on the Ṛgveda and Yajurveda and wrote the Ṛgvedādibhāṣyabhūmikā, teaching that the Saṃhitās alone are revelation, that they teach one God under many names, and that Vedic study is open to all.

name: Sri Aurobindo
summary: U01 contribution: author of The Secret of the Veda, a symbolic-psychological reading of the Ṛgveda.
